Quote (original): Tat ke baal ud gaye the. Sar pe matka dho dho ke. Aur vo bole ki pehle toh tat pe baal hi chale gaye the. Ab baith ke sweater bhunate hoon — apne pote ke liye, apne bachchon ke liye. Nabad mein bahut saare region hain jahan pe ye wale region pe baal nahi hain kyunki matka utha utha ke.
Quote (translated): The hair at the temples had flown away — from carrying the pot on the head. And they said: earlier the hair at the temples had all gone. Now I sit and knit sweaters — for my grandchildren, for my children. In many regions of Nabad, the women in those regions have no hair because of carrying the pot.

Quote (original): So if I say that you came to me and you said that you have this problem, I have a solution for it — aapne khud decide kiya ki mera problem kya hai. Theek hai? Aapko bahar se jo dikha, aapne aur aap aa gaye meri problems ko solve karne ke liye. So I never got interested. Plus, more than interest — jab koi solution provide kiya gaya hota hai toh aap — jiske liye vo solution hai — vo usse kitna attach ho raha hai uss solution se?
Quote (translated): So if I say that you came to me and said you have this problem, I have a solution for it — you yourself decided what my problem is. Right? Whatever you saw from outside, and you came to solve my problems. So I never got interested. Plus, more than interest — when a solution is provided, the person for whom that solution is — how attached are they becoming to that solution?

Quote (original): Aajkal toh ek bhains chali gayi aapda mein toh aap Rs. 10,000 denge toh bhains kharid lijiye.
Quote (translated): Nowadays if a buffalo dies in a disaster they give you Rs. 10,000 and say go buy a buffalo.

Quote (original): 'Hum jis jaati se aate hain na — humare liye koi kuchh nahi karta.' So he said: 'kis scheme se paisa utha raha hai tu, aur kitna uthana hai, aur kahan sign karna hai? Tu mujhe bata, par tu please ye roz aana chhod. Matlab tu dukhi kar diya yaar, 15 din ho gaye tere ko mere — matlab makkhi ki tarah bhinbhina raha hai.' So he said: 'mere ko toh kahin pe sign nahi karana — jab aapka taka banaunga na, tab aapke kagazon pe sign karunga, abhi kahin nahi karana.'
Quote (translated): 'From the community we come from — nobody does anything for us.' So he said: 'Which scheme are you drawing money from, how much do you have to take, and where do I have to sign? You tell me, but please stop coming daily. I mean you have made me miserable — 15 days now — I mean you are buzzing around like a fly.' So he said: 'I don't have to sign anywhere right now — when I build your taka, then I will sign your papers, not anywhere now.'

Quote (original): And he was so sure that this is fake. And he says that: 'yaar aaj tak na jaane kitne log aaye, kitne hi sign karwaye hain, vo paisa kahan ja raha hai, kidhar ja raha hai, nahi pata.' So when we started working there — aaj se chaar saal pehle — vahan pe kuch farm ponds ban rahe the aur ek side hamara project tabhi shuru ho raha tha. Toh there were few people jinhonne kaha ki humne toh ek sarkari scheme chalti hai jismein farm ponds bante hain — toh unhone usme apna naam likhwa rakha tha. So somehow vo awareness create hui aur phir somehow we managed to convince few farmers ki aap apna farm pond banwa lo.
Quote (translated): And he was so sure that this is fake. And he says: 'God knows how many people came till today, how many signatures were taken, where that money is going, nobody knows.' So when we started working there — four years ago — some farm ponds were being built there and on one side our project was starting then. So there were a few people who said: there is a government scheme in which farm ponds are made — so they had already registered their names in it. So somehow that awareness was created and then somehow we managed to convince a few farmers to get their farm pond built.

Quote (original): Pichhle saal Suresh bhai said ki they are saying ki 'aapne humare saare logon ke bana liye.' Are — aapko jo aapko chaar saal pehle banane the, vo humne chaar saal mein dhire-dhire karke bhai — vo log pareshan hue — aur aap free mein bana rahe ho, main 50% contribution le rahi hun. 'Achha 50%' — kisan ke liye mayne rakhta hai. Toh so vo faith lose ho gaya hai logon mein because of the reputation, the kind of work jo chal raha hai.
Quote (translated): Last year Suresh bhai said they are saying: 'You have built for all our people.' Oh — what you should have built four years ago, we built it gradually over four years — they got frustrated — and you are building it for free, I am taking 50% contribution. 'Oh 50%' — it matters to the farmer. So that faith has been lost in people because of the reputation, the kind of work that has been going on.

Quote (original): Abhi dedh lakh ki bhains. Abhi parson ki roz hi apni ek bhains expire ho gayi.
Quote (translated): Right now a buffalo costs one and a half lakh. Just the day before yesterday our own buffalo died.

Quote (original): Toh maine use puchha — Amma, baarish kaisi hui maan se iss baar? Toh bolte hain: 'are laa beta, bahut badhiya, bahut badhiya.' Toh maine kaha: 'bahut badhiya?' Maine kaha nuksaan kitna ho gaya? Bole: 'are bhale hua ho — main aur mehman kate badhiya. Matlab main aur mehman — ye do kismat walon ki kismat mein hote hain.' Matlab someone jiska ghar, ghar ki chhat gir gayi hai, someone jis ab soti hai toh teen tirchi padi hai, us teen ke neeche vo soti hai — aur iski koi guarantee nahi hai ki raat ko baarish nahi hogi. Vo baarish bhi hogi, ye ghar gal jaayega, bah jaayega.
Quote (translated): So I asked her: Amma, how was this rain this time? She says: 'Oh come, beta, very wonderful, very wonderful.' I said: 'very wonderful?' I asked: how much damage happened? She said: 'oh, good it came — water and guest, these are the two things that come only to the fortunate.' Meaning: someone whose house roof has fallen, someone who now sleeps under a charpoy (cot) lying sideways, sleeping under that charpoy — and there is no guarantee that it won't rain at night. It will rain, the house will melt, it will wash away.

Quote (original): Aur mujhe I realized ki — ek aur mahila hai, Shaitan Singh ki wife hai Renu — unke bachcha — vo bahut time se try karte the — unke chaar paanch bachchiyan ho gayi, kuch miscarriages ho gaye — aur he is financially bahut struggle kar rahe the. Uske beta hua. Aur when I got to know ki Shaitan Singh ke beta hua, main bahut khush thi. And I hardly know him. Aur then uske saat din ka tha uska bachcha — aur bahut tezi din baarish hui thi — uska ghar gal gaya. Uski saat aath saal ki bachchi thi, vo ghar ke bahar paavda leke khadi thi ki kaise bhi mitti ka ek dher kar dun ki bahar ka paani ghar ke andar nahi aaye. Ghar gal raha tha.
Quote (translated): And I realized — there is another woman, Shaitan Singh's wife, Renu — her child — they had been trying for a long time — they had four or five daughters, some miscarriages happened — and he is financially very struggling. She had a son. And when I got to know that Shaitan Singh had a son, I was very happy. And I hardly know him. And then the child was seven days old — and it rained heavily that day — his house melted. His seven to eight year old daughter was standing outside the house with a shovel trying somehow to pile up mud so that the water from outside doesn't come inside. The house was melting.

Quote (original): Toh I realized ki humare paas sab kuchh hai aur phir bhi ye cheezen humein pareshan karti hain. Kaise maine har region mein puchha aur har koi pareshan tha. Main bhi pareshan tha — mere bhi mujhe bhi pareshani hui jab baarish hui thi. Lekin uss mahila ka sab kuchh bah gaya — par vo pareshan nahi thi. She was thinking ki 'main shukra — main kismat vali hun ki mere ghar mehman aaye.' Kyunki vo nature ko kabhi tokna nahi chahte.
Quote (translated): So I realized: we have everything and yet these things bother us. How — I asked in every region and everyone was troubled. I was troubled too — even I was troubled when it rained. But that woman's everything had washed away — yet she was not troubled. She was thinking: 'I am grateful — I am fortunate that guests came to my home.' Because they never want to interrupt nature.

Quote (original): Vo nature ko — it's like it's the beauty na ki nature — maan ke maan ka gussa bhi hota hai aur maan ka pyaar bhi hota hai. Ab maan ka pyaar toh lena chahte ho par maan ka gussa nahi lena chahte — jo ek saath bahut saari baarish hui, vo ho sakta hai maan ka gussa ho. Par they are ready for it.
Quote (translated): They treat nature — it's like it's the beauty, isn't it — nature — a mother's anger also happens and a mother's love also happens. Now you want to take the mother's love but don't want to take the mother's anger — the rain that came all at once, that could be the mother's anger. But they are ready for it.

Quote (original): Till the time hum ek dusre ko thoda-thoda space den, aur ek dusre ke liye aur vo space den trust build up karne ke liye — toh I think that is one thing that I want every place. Even with nature — hum mujhe lagta hai ki humein thoda sa space deke sochna chahie ki is it really a disaster, ya ye hamara fault hai, ya there is something that we need to fix. So I think there is space and that space builds trust. Space builds everything.
Quote (translated): Till the time we give each other a little space, and give each other that space to build trust — I think that is one thing that I want every place. Even with nature — I feel we need to give a little space and think: is it really a disaster, or is this our fault, or is there something that we need to fix. So I think there is space and that space builds trust. Space builds everything.

Quote (original): Aur ya — aur phir ye mahilaon ke dimaag ko shant karta hai. Aaj agar mera padosi hai jo mujhe 24 ghante keh raha hai ki 'yaar tera beta vahin padha rehta hai' — aur vahi hai jo mujhe ye keh rahe hain ki 'yaar meri teacher ne bola hai ki mere bachche ne bahut achha kiya.' I feel proud, I feel happy. As a mother, as a women — mera physical stress kam ho gaya, toh main vaise bhi khush hoon. Toh now I have time — time to do things that I like.
Quote (translated): And yes — and then this calms women's minds. Today if my neighbour is telling me 24 hours: 'your son just sits around there' — and they are the same ones who say to me: 'the teacher said my child did very well.' I feel proud, I feel happy. As a mother, as a woman — my physical stress has reduced, so I am happy anyway. So now I have time — time to do things that I like.

Quote (original): The kids are getting the sense of good and bad. Aur isske saath mein hi ye jo aap jab bachchon ke result achchhe aate hain, bachchon mein improvement aata hai, bachche kam bimaar padte hain — in sab ka asar maan ke upar padta hai. Mera bachcha khush hai toh main khush hun. Mera pati khush hai toh main khush hun. Mere sasur healthy hain, kam bimariyan hain. Toh ye sab kuchh lekar aa raha hai — mere physical stress ko kam kiya hai.
Quote (translated): The kids are getting the sense of good and bad. And alongside this — when children's results improve, there is improvement in children, children fall ill less — all of this affects the mother. My child is happy so I am happy. My husband is happy so I am happy. My in-laws are healthy, fewer illnesses. So all of this brings — it has reduced my physical stress.

Quote (original): Haan, dedh lakh rupaye kitni chahiye. Ek mahine ke baad mein vo pyarthi. Do din uske thoda normal si tabiyat kharab rahi — teesre roz uske check up bhi karaya — aadhe ghante baad mein doctor.
Quote (translated): Yes, a buffalo costs one and a half lakh. She was due to deliver (be with calf) in a month. For two days she was a little unwell — on the third day had her checked up — half an hour later the doctor (said she was gone).

Quote (original): Yahan ka paani, yahan ka jo belt hai na, ye pura belt hai — ismen paani bahut khara hai. So yahan pe ye ek aur matlab yahan ka bada problem hai. So jo log afford kar sakte hain, vo water filters laga lete hain, but ek bada chunk hai jo nahi kar pata. Toh vo log usi paani ko peete hain.
Quote (translated): The water here — the belt that this region is in — throughout this belt the water is very brackish. So this is another big problem here. Those who can afford it get water filters installed, but there is a big chunk that cannot. So those people drink that same water.

Quote (original): Toh uske dauran hum baat kar rahe the toh bahut saari mahilaon ne bataya ki vahan pe paani khara aata hai jiski vajah se bachchon ke daant peele ho jaate hain — toh bachche bahut chhoti umr mein muskurana avoid karne lag jaate hain. Thinking that people will make fun of them.
Quote (translated): So during that, we were talking and many women told us that the water there is brackish because of which children's teeth become yellow — so children at a very young age start avoiding smiling. Thinking that people will make fun of them.

Quote (original): Vahan pe mahilaen — purush dono hi bahut kamjor hain zyada. Matlab jab aap 50-55 cross kar jaate ho — vahan pe buzurg hafte mein ek baar nahaate hain. Paani itna kha raha hai ki jis din nahaate hain us din poore sharir mein dard hota hai aur khujli hoti hai. Aur haddiyan kamjor hain — saare buzurgon ke aap dekhenge pair aise tirche hain.
Quote (translated): There — both women and men are very weak. Meaning when you cross 50–55 — the elderly there bathe once a week. The water is so corrosive that on the day they bathe, their entire body aches and itches. And bones are weak — you will see all the elderly's legs are bent and crooked.

Quote (original): Aur mahilaen — mujhe ek din hansi aayi — hamara ek survey tha uss din mera. Main gayi toh main ek mahila ko dhundh rahi thi — toh usne kaha ki vahan ek khat padi thi, khat pe ek chadar padi thi. Toh main uss ghar ke aage se kam se kam chhah se saat baar nikli. Aur phir thodi der baad maine ek uncle se puchha — maine kaha aaj masa nahi dikhai de rahe. Bole haan, vo so rahe hain. Maine kaha kahan so rahe hain — andar toh main gayi thi, andar nahi dikhi. Bole aapke peeche hai na — vo mahila aisi ho ke so rahi thi aur mujhe laga ki vo chadar padi hai koi.
Quote (translated): And women — I laughed one day — we had a survey that day. I went and was looking for a woman — someone said there is a cot there with a sheet on it. And I passed in front of that house at least six to seven times. Then after a while I asked an uncle: I haven't seen the masa (auntie) today. He said yes, she is sleeping. I asked where is she sleeping — I had gone inside, didn't see her inside. He said: she is behind you — that woman was lying curled up like that and I had thought it was just a sheet lying there.

Quote (original): Vo itne se ho gaye hain — unki bodies vo fold ho jaate hain ekdam aise — kyunki with time unke bones, unki haddiyan itni zyada kamjor ho gayi hain. Aur unhen budhapa bahut jaldi aa jaata hai. Ye badi dikkat hai. Kyunki males ka phir bhi movement hota hai — mahilaen sirf ghar ghar mein rehti hain.
Quote (translated): They have become so small — their bodies fold up completely — because over time their bones have become so weak. And old age comes to them very fast. This is a big problem. Because men at least have movement — women just stay within the house.

Quote (original): Toh ye phir — when I ask them ki agar aapke sharir mein dikkat hai toh aap doctor ko kyon nahi dikhate — and she said ki dekho, par 30 tak toh humein khalta hai kyunki 21-22 saal ki shaadi karke aate hain toh dusre ghar se aate hain toh yahan ka paani khara lagta hai. So chhah saat saal tak toh hum bolte hain. Kyunki mehsoos hota hai. Uske baad mein normalize ho jaate hain. Uske baad mein vo bhul jaate hain ki normal kya tha. This is that — this becomes their new normal.
Quote (translated): So then — when I ask them: if there is a problem in your body why don't you see a doctor — and she said: look, till 30 we notice it because we come from another home after marriage at 21–22 and here the water tastes brackish. So for six to seven years we say something. Because we feel it. After that we normalize. After that they forget what normal was. This is that — this becomes their new normal.

Quote (original): That's it. Every aspect like — mera pashu swasth hai — se leke domestic violence aur bahut saari aisi cheezen jo mental health. Paani aa gaya isliye mental health theek ho gayi hai. So people are not able to connect. But jab hum paani ki baat karte hain — ye pura ek chakra hai. Aur paani mool hai har cheez ka. Vo center mein baitha hai — aur vo dikhai nahi deta — lekin vo har cheez mein hissa hai.
Quote (translated): That's it. Every aspect — from: my livestock is healthy — to domestic violence and many things like mental health. Water came so mental health improved. People are not able to connect these. But when we talk about water — it is a complete cycle. And water is the root of everything. It sits at the center — and it is invisible — but it is part of everything.

Quote (original): Paani leke vapas aati hai, uske ghor vapas aa jaate hain, phir vo paani peene pilaane mein lag jaati hai, aur shaam ke khane mein aur sab kuchh lag jaati hai — aur by the time vo un sab se free ho ke usko shaam ka paani laane ka time hota hai, tab tak late ho jaata hai. Toh jab late ho jaata hai toh husband vapas aa jaata hai. Aur jab husband vapas aate hain, vo thake haare aate hain. Aur unhen wife bhi kehti hai — kyunki ab vo bhi thak chuki hai, usne bhi kaam kiya — toh vo yeh kehti hai ki aap paani le aao.
Quote (translated): She comes back with water, the livestock return, then she is occupied with giving everyone water to drink, and in the evening meal and everything — and by the time she is free from all that and it is time for her to go for evening water, it is already late. So when it is late the husband has come back. And when the husband comes back, he comes back tired and exhausted. And the wife also says — because she is also tired now, she has also worked — so she says: you please bring water.

Quote (original): Toh vo jab glass matke mein daalta hai aur matka khali hota hai toh use gussa aata hai. Vo kehti hai ki paani laane ka samay nahi mila — aur sab jawab ek hi hai ki 'pure din padhe-padhe kiya tha?' Hai na? Aur vo uska maanna — matlab — vo aadmi itna frustrate ho jaata hai kyunki vo thaka hua hai. Mahila ki thakan nazar nahi aa rahi hai. Purush thaka hua hai, vo itna frustrate ho jaata hai ki vo haath uthata hai ya uske bas mein jo bhi hai — vo bartan phenk ta hai, vo jo sab kuchh karta hai.
Quote (translated): So when he tries to pour water into the glass from the pot and the pot is empty, he gets angry. She says: I didn't get time to bring water — and the only response is: 'What were you doing all day sitting around?' Right? And he believes it — meaning — that man is so frustrated because he is tired. The woman's exhaustion is not visible. The man is tired, he gets so frustrated that he raises his hand or does whatever is in his power — he throws utensils, he does all of that.

Quote (original): Aaj usmein vishesh jo problem hai dikkat Ram Swaroop ji keh rahe hain. Problem hai ki dekhiye, jab sarkar aankde karti hai toh kehti hai ki 'hum itne hazaar karod kisanon ko beej ke liye itne arab rupaye baante hain.' Aap ek per vyakti nikaal ke dekhiye bata dijiye. Zyada se zyada hoga ek do sau rupaye per kisan ko. Aur per kisan ko aur kitna — ek gaon ko kitna divide karte hain — ek hazaar rupaye — aur ek hazaar rupaye is gaon mein kitne kisan honge? Toh ek thaili pandrah logon ke liye hoga. 10 logon, 15 logon ke liye — bas. Haan bas — yeh hamara aankara kya jaata hai ki humne kisaanon ko itne arab rupaye bhi de diya. Bas bhai baat — achha — ek vyakti ke liye kitna aapne bheja paisa? Toh vo problem ye hai.
Quote (translated): Today the specific problem Ram Swaroop ji is talking about — the problem is: look, when the government gives statistics it says 'we distribute this many thousand crore rupees for seeds to this many lakh farmers.' You calculate per person and tell me. At most it would be one to two hundred rupees per farmer. And per farmer — how much is divided for one village — a thousand rupees — and in a thousand rupees how many farmers are in this village? So one bag will be for fifteen people. For 10 people, 15 people — that's it. Yes that's it — and what figure goes out from us: 'we distributed this many billion rupees to farmers.' That's it brother — good — but how much money per person did you send? That is the problem.

Quote (original): Ki tu number likh rahi hai — matlab abhi hum baat kar rahe the na ki number toh ho jaate hain par vo vo stories pe hum nahi dhyan dete. And she — itna gyan kisi ko kaise ho sakta hai? Mujhe bahut chhota mehsoos hua. I felt like — is mahila ko pata hai, ye mujhe itne saal se jaanti hai, ye TBS ko itne saal se jaanti hai. Ye mujhse pehle TBS ko jaanti hai — jab se maine jaana, usse pehle se — aur use pata hai ki main vo miss kar rahi hun jo sabse important hai.
Quote (translated): You are writing numbers — meaning, right now we were talking about: numbers happen, but we don't pay attention to those stories. And her — how can anyone have so much wisdom? I felt very small. I felt like — this woman knows, she has known me for years, she has known TBS for years. She knew TBS before I knew it — and she knows that I am missing what is most important.

Quote (original): Aur I main bolti hun na — main har baar jab field pe jaati hun na, toh mujhe koi na koi aisa mil jaata hai jo itna kuch sikha ke jaata hai. Kai baar toh life lessons mil jaate hain. It is one of the life lessons for me ki ek mahila ko kitna gyan hai — matlab uski koi seema hi nahi hai. Ye jaante hain — ya sochte hain ki hum kyunki school gaye the toh jo school gaye the so called education, humein pata hai. Par uss mahila ne meri aankhen khol di.
Quote (translated): And I say — every time I go to the field, I find someone who teaches me so much before they leave. Many times I get life lessons. It is one of the life lessons for me — how much wisdom a woman has — there is simply no limit to it. We think — or think that because we went to school, the so-called education that those who went to school have, we know. But that woman opened my eyes.

Quote (original): Vahi badha wala system chhe. Haan. Koi toh kachro bin wala chhe, koi bhi aisa mein sab wala chhe.
Quote (translated): That is the same old (inequality) system. Yes. Someone is the one who picks garbage, someone has everything.

Quote (original): Ab bachchon ke nahane dhone, ghar mein paani aane ka bachchon ke concentration badhne se kya kya connection hai? The connection is ki uske ghar pe paani hai, toh ab uski maan ko bahar nahi jaana pad raha. Toh maan ko dikh raha hai ki are yaar mera bachcha ganda hai — toh main use nila dhula ke — ab vo jo bachcha pehle uske paas mein koi nahi baithta tha kyunki teri mein se badbu aati hai — ab log uske paas mein baithte hain. Vo aage baithta hai — pehle vo peeche baithta tha sabse alag kyunki use sharam aati thi ki main ganda hoon, mere mein se badbu aati hai. Vo aage baithta hai, vo dhyan deta hai, usko sunai deta hai sab kuch jo teacher bol raha hota hai. He is interested.
Quote (translated): Now, the washing of children and water coming home to children's concentration improving — what is the connection? The connection is: there is water at home, so now the mother doesn't have to go outside. So the mother sees: my child is dirty — so she cleans and washes the child — now that child, earlier nobody would sit near him because he smelled — now people sit near him. He sits in the front — earlier he sat at the back, separate from everyone, because he was ashamed: I am dirty, I smell. He sits in front, he pays attention, he can hear everything the teacher says. He is interested.

Quote (original): Bachchiyan school jaane lagi hain kyunki ghar mein paani hai — us bachchi ko school skip karne ki zaroorat nahi hai, bachchiyan school ja rahi hain, apni padhai puri kar rahi hain. Bachchiyon ki jaldi shaadi hoti thi kyunki bahut early age mein vo paani bharne ke liye schools chhod dete the. Aur phir ek point aata tha ki — kyunki padhai toh kar nahi rahi — jab bachchiyan kehti hain ki 'padhai hamare liye jaldi shaadi na ho jaane ka ek zariya hai jisse main maan-baap ko rok sakti hoon.' Agar log samajhdar hain, agar maan-baap samajhdar hain, toh vo apne maan-baap ko rok sakti hain ki mujhe jaldi shaadi nahi karni. Nahi toh unhen sirf vo umr dikhai deti hai — 16 saal ki ho gayi, 13 saal ki ho gayi, 14 saal ki ho gayi.
Quote (translated): Girls have started going to school because there is water at home — that girl doesn't need to skip school, girls are going to school, completing their studies. Girls were getting married early because from a very young age they would drop out of school to fetch water. And then there came a point — because she is not studying — when girls say: 'education for us is a means to prevent early marriage — it is a way with which I can stop my parents.' If the parents are wise, they can be stopped: I don't want to get married early. Otherwise they only see that age — she is 16 now, she is 13, she is 14.

Quote (original): Jab jo bachchiyan ghar baithi hain, lekin jo school ja rahi hain, jo padhai likhai kar rahi hain — unka dimaag umr pe nahi jaata, unka dhyan class pe hota hai. Dasvi ho gayi, gyarvi ho gayi, barvi ho gayi — ab bachchi college jaayegi, and they feel proud. Aur ye hota hai ki meri jaise — abhi main gayi toh ek mahila ne bola ki meri bachchi gaon mein sabse zyada padhi-likhi bachchi hai. She was proud — and otherwise hota ye ki 'are gaon mein sabse badi bachchi hai jiski shaadi nahi hui ab tak.' Toh vahi proud vahi unke sharm mein badal jaata hai ki 'yaar teri beti itni badi ho gayi abhi tak teri shaadi nahi hui.' So this is what happened.
Quote (translated): The girls who are sitting at home — but those who are going to school, who are studying — their mind doesn't go to age, their attention is on the class. Tenth done, eleventh done, twelfth done — now the girl will go to college, and they feel proud. And this happens like — just now when I went, one woman said: my daughter is the most educated girl in the village. She was proud — and otherwise what would happen is: 'oh, she is the oldest girl in the village and not yet married.' So that same pride would turn into their shame: 'your daughter has grown so big and still not married.' So this is what happened.

Quote (original): Isski vajah se jaise vo amma ne bola na — so now if I connect — ki ab vo apne bachchon ko school nila dhula ke bhejti hai, ab vo din mein rest karti hai. Uss rest ke baad mein — she is not stressed out, vo thaki hui nahi hai. Toh jab uske bachche ghar aate hain, toh jab vo unhen khana khila rahi hoti hai, toh vo khush hain. Toh vo khush hai toh vo unse unke bare mein puchhegi. Vo bachche jo bol rahe hain vo uss pe gussa nahi hogi — vo ek healthy relation banati hai apne bachchon ke saath mein.
Quote (translated): Because of this, as that amma said — so now if I connect — now she sends her children to school washed and clean, now she rests during the day. After that rest — she is not stressed out, she is not exhausted. So when her children come home, when she is feeding them, they are happy. So she is happy, so she will ask them about themselves. She will not get angry at what the children say — she builds a healthy relationship with her children.

Quote (original): Vo nahi humein dikhai deta. Hum use paani se connect nahi karte. Par jab maan aur bachche achchhe se baat karte hain, ek healthy communication hota hai — bachche apni baatein share karte hain apne maata-pita ke saamne. Wives ki lives easy ho jaati hain. Husband wife ke relations achchhe ho jaate hain.
Quote (translated): This is not visible to us. We don't connect it with water. But when mother and children communicate well, there is healthy communication — children share their things with their parents. Wives' lives become easier. Husband-wife relations improve.

Quote (original): Jab bachchon pe mata-pita ka dhyan nahi rehta toh bachche apne — de want someone to spend time with — spend more time with kids of the same age. Aur usually jo bachche school nahi ja rahe hote, unhen 24/7 pata hai ki ye school nahi jaata toh ye toh mil hi jaata hai. In conversation leads the child to bahut usual — words use karna, language — internet ka access aajkal sabke paas hai. Toh jin logon ke ghar pe paani tanka bana, un gharon ke bachchon ki bhasha mein badlav dekha gaya.
Quote (translated): When parents don't pay attention to children, the children want someone to spend time with — they spend more time with kids of the same age. And usually the children who are not going to school, they know 24/7 that this kid doesn't go to school, so this one is always available. This conversation leads the child toward using very usual bad words, bad language — internet access everyone has nowadays. So in the homes where a water tanka was built, a change was noticed in the language of the children of those houses.

Quote (original): Nahi ole ole dhundh pade aapne toh.
Quote (translated): No, we got fog and hailstones — you did get those then.

Quote (original): Unke paas kaiyon ke jo karte the unke paas ho gaya khatam — aaj unki boring bhi nahi hai.
Quote (translated): Those who used to do this — their water got finished — today they don't even have a borewell.

Quote (original): Aata si baisa hoon toh kahala do kilo doodh de rahe ho toh bas ek sau bees ko doodh deko. Ek sau bees bade malle se maan. Ek sau bees mein dhoop mein aa jaaye. Ek sau bees ko do kilo doodh dete hain. Raat mein phir aange jaaye jaaye. Saath din mein na do baje toh dhoop mein aa jaaye vahan se phir.
Quote (translated): When I used to come to sit, they'd say — you give two kilos of milk — so just look at 120 (rupees) for milk. 120 is considered a big amount there. For 120 you come out in the heat. For 120 we give two kilos of milk. At night they'd go and go again. In seven days — by two o'clock — you'd have to come back out into the heat from there again.

Quote (original): Gaon mein toh vahan kabhi aisa hua ki bachchon ki padhai chhudwani padi?
Quote (translated): In the village — did it ever happen that the children's studies had to be stopped?

Quote (original): Nahi nahi aisi lo pato nahi de. Nahi toh dekho ma'am sarkari mein phataaya. Thaan bataun.
Quote (translated): No no, nothing like that. No — look ma'am we got them educated in government schools. Let me tell you.

Quote (original): Suru suru regular jab laga toh private mein padhaya ja. Chahe apan aaj na lagi na fees toh jaal do mahine baad fees de diya ja ne. Hun. Pade aati nau pat khona hai bhai.
Quote (translated): Right from the start, regularly when it could be arranged, we sent them to private school. Even if we couldn't manage today, we'd give the fees two months later. Yes. Education has to come brother, or you'll be ruined.

Quote (original): Bachche phataayegi pe shaadi gaddiya laag lagaayegi.
Quote (translated): Had to educate the children and had to bear the expenses of weddings too.

Quote (original): Aata pe te jaana chhe desu ko chalo khabali gaye ka toh doodh liye. Ye to hajo khava ek ulta ek baant khava kisi se. Ek taan aapdaan chhopdi roti khavaan. Ek loo ki roti khavaan.
Quote (translated): For flour we had to go to Desu and others — if the cow went somewhere we'd take the milk. For eating — just eating whatever was available, sharing a bite with someone. Eating one thin roti of your own. Eating one hot (loo-cooked) roti.

Quote (original): Are bhai, koi ki koi parivar ke hi log — matlab parivar ke jaise hamare chacha ji vagairah the na — ek sarkari karmachari tha chacha. Wo university mein toh vo yahan matlab boring karwa ke hod bana ke gaon mein pipeline leke hai na — toh wo humare ko paani bhi nahi bharne deta tha. Ye condition thi hamari.
Quote (translated): Oh brother — it was family people themselves — like our uncle and others — one uncle was a government employee. He got a borewell drilled, built a tank, laid a pipeline in the village — and he wouldn't even let us fill water. This was our condition.

Quote (original): Ye road aap hi jaate the toh aap hi jaate the. Haan ye road ne dekh lete hai. Bhag gharan dekh lo agar bigar manne par badhiya paani. Ye maan le maine koti chal par bhagon diya paani. Phir bhi mala ho ja. Phir bhi mala bhi aakhde ja bhai aath. Main toh light ek hoon na hi.
Quote (translated): You yourself used to go on this road, you yourself would go. Yes, one can see through this road. Run from the house — look, if it breaks open (the water source opens) there is good water. Say I poured water running on the big tank. Even then it fills up. Even then it barely fills up to eight (units). I am just one person for the light (electricity).

Quote (original): Toh li ta bat na leya jao ch. Te jaan baat naal se bhai light aa jao te baag motor chal jao toh bhale ho paani. Ani kon pe ba de de to kon pe ba de ja. Pe saari kaali tanker mangwa. Pe tanker chale chale na. Pe tanker mangwa ta pe.
Quote (translated): So take that one and go. When brother, when electricity comes and the motor runs then good — there is water. And then who puts it here, who puts it there. The whole night ordering a tanker. Whether the tanker came or not. Order a tanker then.

Quote (original): Ghee vagairah sab. Phir uske baad maine ye bhains vagairah lai. Toh aaram se khud ka doodh hota hai aur yahan se Rs. 80 liter mein dairy mein bhi jata hai sarkari mein. Kabhi 75 kabhi Rs. 80, Rs. 5 extra milta hai kilo pe.
Quote (translated): Ghee and everything. Then after that I brought buffalo and all. So comfortably we have our own milk and from here it also goes to the government dairy at Rs. 80 per litre. Sometimes Rs. 75, sometimes Rs. 80 — Rs. 5 extra per kg is also given.

Quote (original): Ghee achha mil raha hai, shuddh khana mil raha hai aur khud ghee hai na, gehun, sabziyan — khud hi aap.
Quote (translated): Good ghee is available, pure food is available, and we have our own ghee, wheat, vegetables — all ourselves.

Quote (original): Kuchh nahi mila. Agar aaya bhi hai na toh ye beech wale hi hai na — jo milne wale hain woh hi le gaye apne paas. Aur vo hai jo vo corona ke liye apan ko samjhati thi, bhi rehti thi — bhai parivar se aisa rehna hai, aisa rehna hai, saaf sukhda rakhna hai, kaanda peena hai, dawai lena hai, ye goli lena hai. Unki vishesh doctor hai, Sani Dara Toor — toh vo poori batati rehti thi ki aisa rehna hai.
Quote (translated): Got nothing. Whatever came — the middlemen took it for themselves — those who were meant to get it took it for themselves. And there was that one who used to explain to us about Corona, who used to stay — brother, stay like this with the family, stay like this, keep clean, drink onion water, take medicine, take this pill. Their particular doctor — Sani Dara Toor — she used to keep telling everything about how to stay (healthy).

Quote (original): Bahut hi badhiya. Kha bhi rahe hain, sell bhi kar rahe hain. Abhi jaise maan lo teen lakh ki fasal maine gehun vagairah taiyar karke piya.
Quote (translated): Excellent. We are both eating and selling. Right now, for instance, I have prepared and sold wheat and other crops worth about three lakh rupees.

Quote (original): Sita ji ke chehre mein muskaan aur raunak hamesha rehti hai kaam se kyonki inko laga ki ye khud ka kaam hai. Jab aap khud khada ho jaata hai toh aapki badlav nischit aata hai. Aur pehle tanaav tha, jaana padta tha — abhi apne.
Quote (translated): Sita ji's face always has a smile and radiance from this work — because she felt that this was her own work. When you stand up on your own feet, change is certain to come. And earlier there was tension, she had to go out — but now it's hers.

Quote (original): Tension hai mujhe matlab itna ho jaate hai.
Quote (translated): The tension I had — it used to affect me that much.

Quote (original): Main bata raha hun 27 saal se ye banjar padi thi. Toh 20 saal toh usne kar diya, 3 saal ye, aur 4 saal pehle NREGA chali nahi thi.
Quote (translated): I am telling you — this land had been lying barren for 27 years. So she did 20 years of NREGA, then 3 years this, and 4 years ago the NREGA wasn't running either.

Quote (original): Tractor yahan se crab mein karke trolley mein baith ke jaate hain. Phir vo paanch rupaye tractor wale ko dete hain phir sau rupaye pachhaas pachanav rupaye inke milte hain — aisa tha.
Quote (translated): From here they would sit in the tractor trolley and go. Then they would give five rupees to the tractor driver, and they would get 100, 50, 95 rupees — that was the situation.

Quote (original): Vo bhi nahi thi hamare paas tanki bhi nahi banati thi vaise nahi thi na. To paani agar laate the to vo baaltiyon mein jaise ye tanki mein hi bharte.
Quote (translated): We didn't have that either — the tank wouldn't be built like that, it wasn't there. So if we brought water we would fill it in buckets — like filling this tank.

Quote (original): Haan sunaya nahi — mere yahan pe jaati bhi hai log baag, kahin hai — abhi apne Ramgarh se doosron ka ladka gaya tha jo pehle yeh apne khajano ki rashmi murti moolya mein kaam karta tha. Usko koi laalach deke aur koi bhej diya ki sahab Dubai ki wahan pe woh — wahan pe gaye toh wahan pe woh bakriyan chara raha hai, jaise apne yahan pe bakri jaanwar charate — unke goti oti saaf kar raha hai — yeh kaam kar raha hai. Ab wahan se badi mushkil se woh aaya hai, woh keh raha tha ki wahan pe zindagi narak hai.
Quote (translated): Yes I haven't just heard about it — people from here go too — there is a case — just recently a boy from Ramgarh went — who earlier worked here in some craft or value-based work. Someone lured him and sent him saying: sir, in Dubai there — going there he is now grazing goats there — just like grazing goats and animals here — cleaning their pens and sheds — doing this work. Now he has come back from there with great difficulty — he was saying that life there is hell.

Quote (original): Ki vo kyon nikli, kyon usko adhikar hona? Kay ka adhikar hai? Adhikar kya cheez hoti hai? Tumhen pata nahi hai ki duniya aisi hai. Tum gharon mein usmen bahar nikal rahe ho. Vo bhi ek sochne ka tareeka hai. Hum ye nahi aur vo bhi hai, vo bhi sahi hai. Lekin ye bhi toh ho sakta hai kya hamara samaj surakshit hai nahi ki hum?
Quote (translated): Why did she go out, why should she have that right? What kind of right is it? What is a right anyway? Don't you know the world is like this. You are stepping outside from within your homes. That is also a way of thinking. We don't say that — and that view also exists, that is also valid. But can it also be possible — is our society safe, or are we—?

Quote (original): Ye bhi koi nahi hai. Ho rahi hai kai logon ke saath mein. Jaise maan lo yahan se behrai hoi hai aap Dubai jao — ab aapko wahan company mein ek job milegi. Lekin wahan pe jaake bakriyan chalani padti hai. Gutter saaf karne padte hain. Aisi bahut vahinkar condition ho rahi hai kai logon ke saath mein.
Quote (translated): That (broker/middleman type) is also not here. It is happening with many people. Like say a deaf/deceiving person says: you go to Dubai — now you'll get a job there in a company. But going there you have to tend goats. You have to clean gutters. Such very shameful conditions are happening with many people.

Quote (original): Kyonki ek baar aapne paani ko pakad liya toh aapne bahut saare aayam aap pakad lete hain.
Quote (translated): Because once you have a handle on water, you have a grip on many other dimensions as well.

Quote (original): Pani dikhta nahi hai kyonki vo paisa nahi hai na.
Quote (translated): Water is not visible as capital because it is not money.

Quote (original): Beech mein na toh aapka kuchh sign bhi nahi karenge — vo koi koi mukadma kar de toh bhai phans jaaye. Kuchh sign nahi karte beech mein. Itne chatur aadmi hain. Aapke kha gaye, mere kha gaye. Toh ab vo hamari ye jangir hai na — sab motorcycle pe chal rahe hain aaj bhi. Vo saale Fortuner score mein bhi chal rahe hain. Aur jameeno bhi jameeno bhi kar li unhone — khud ki jameene bacha li aur logon ki kha kha ke aaj four wheeler mein chal rahe hain. Aur badhiya office bana ke jaise Mahindra World City mein office bana liye property ka, AC mein baithe. Gareebon ki kha kha ye condition hai.
Quote (translated): In the middle they won't sign anything — if someone files a case against them, brother, they'd be trapped. They don't sign anything in between. Such clever people. They ate yours, they ate mine. So now those in our Jangid community — they're all still on motorcycles. Those scoundrels are driving Fortuners. And they grabbed lands too — saved their own lands and eating others', today they drive four-wheelers. Built nice offices like a property office in Mahindra World City — sitting in AC. Eating the poor — this is the condition.

Quote (original): Jo bhi jo jo likh raha hai. Jaise maan lo maine 50,000 laaya aur 50,000 bola chhah mahine mein de dunga — nahi mili — laakar mere jaanvar bhaans khol denge bhaiya — bhaans de denge.
Quote (translated): Whatever is written. Say I brought 50,000 and said I'll return 50,000 in six months — if not given — they'll come and open my buffalo's tether — they'll take the buffalo.

Quote (original): Nahi, kapde pehne hi kyon the isne?
Quote (translated): No — why did she wear those clothes at all?

Quote (original): Kapde aise pehne
Quote (translated): She wore such clothes—

Quote (original): Toh uss daur mein unni sau pachhattar pachhasi mein jab paani ka yeh gyaan tantra ek tareeke se jis par dhool jam chuki thi aur usko phir hum dobara se Arun Bharat Sangh ne usko jaagrit kiya aur Johar Tokhar Pagare aise purane purane naam jo kahin sarkari kitabon mein dab chuke the unko phir se unko ubhara aur un naamon ko bolne mein gaurav kiya nahi toh ye ho ki sahab gaon mein johar hai toh bolne mein bhi sharmati thi johar kya hota hai nahi nahi lekin vo gaurav kyon hai usko vo kaam shuru kiya.
Quote (translated): So in that era, between 1975 and '85, when this knowledge-system about water had gathered dust — Tarun Bharat Sangh revived it. Old names like Johar, Tokhar, Pagare — which had been buried somewhere in government books — were revived, and dignity was given to speaking these names. Otherwise what would happen — if there is a 'johar' (traditional pond) in the village, people were even embarrassed to say it. What is a johar? No no — but why is it something to be proud of? That work was begun.

Quote (original): Ek nayi water policy aati hai jismein pehli baar paani ko as a commodity ghoshit karne ki koshish ki gayi tab humein laga ki Tarun Bharat Sangh ko laga ki agar paani commodity ghoshit kar diya jata hai toh yani uska khareedna aur bechaana bahut aasaan ho jata hai. Achha aur ye khareed aur bechaana sirf paani ke botal tak uski us tak seemit nahi thi ki sahab vo kisi ne das rupaye ka vo theek hai vo le rahe hain. Ye ismein phir saare nadi, naale vo sab include ho jaate hain. Matlab aap bade se bade tala kisi ko bhi bech sakte hain. Bade se badi bechne ka matlab koi aise bheche nahi jaate lekin haan unke adhikar ka upyog agar aapne unko upyog ka adhikar kisi ek vyakti vishesh ya company vishesh ko de diya toh commodity jaise shabdon ke aane se vo bahut aasaan ho jata hai. Ye hua ki nahi ye toh sahi nahi hai toh yani phir humein laga ki policy pe bhi kaam karna padega iss tarah ke agar hum pata hai matlab ye toh privatization of water resources ko ko ja raha hai. Toh ek chhota sa shabd kis tarike se ek chhota sa shabd aap ek usko natural resource se aap usko commodity bhi kar dete hain, commodity se phir vahi cheez vo kaise privatization ka raasta khul jata hai.
Quote (translated): A new water policy came, in which for the first time an attempt was made to declare water as a commodity. Then it struck Tarun Bharat Sangh: if water is declared a commodity, then buying and selling it becomes very easy. And this buying and selling was not limited to a bottle of water — like someone buying a ten-rupee bottle, that's okay. All rivers, all streams get included in this. Meaning you can sell the biggest lake to anyone. Selling the biggest doesn't mean physically selling — but if you give usage rights over it to a particular individual or a particular company, then with words like 'commodity' that becomes very easy. This happened — this is not right — meaning we then felt we would also have to work on policy, because this was heading towards privatization of water resources. So this is how a small word — just a small word — can turn a natural resource into a commodity, and from commodity, how the path to privatization opens up.

Quote (original): Ki agar hamari nadiyan hi jinda nahi hongi agar wo aviral aur nirbhar nahi hongi agar nadiyon ki hi zameenon ko hathiya liya jayega toh phir yeh toh hum jis sabhyata aur jinse hum badi badi baatein karte hain wo jeevit bachenge hi kaisi theek hai na. Nadi ko point A se point B tak ke beh ke beech mein bahne wale paani ki tarah agar sirf utna hi aap dekhenge toh toh khatam ho jaayega aur jis desh mein aap aap kareeb karodon logon ki aastha Ganga jaise paani se judi hui ho. Aur mujhe lagta hai ki theek hai ek baar ko tum aastha aur vo sabko bhi hum side mein rakhte hain ek baar. Lekin sawal yeh uthta hai ki nadi jis zameen par behti hai. Voh toh uski hai. Aapko kisne adhikar diya ki uski uski jameen ko kisi aur mein kisi aur ko dene ka. Ya ki sahab vo 100 meter hai toh usko 5 meter hai toh theek hai yahan hum apartment bana lete hain aur aap nadiyon ko sikodte sikodte sikodte aap unko nala bana dete hain. Aur phir jab baadh aa jati hai toh phir aap shor machate hain. Toh iss tarah ke sawal toh iss tarah se Tarun Bharat Singh talab se nadi tak pahuncha.
Quote (translated): If our rivers are not alive, if they are not perennial and free-flowing, if the land of the rivers itself is encroached upon — then this civilization we speak so grandly about, how will it survive? If you look at a river only as water flowing from point A to point B, it will be finished. And in a country where hundreds of millions of people's faith is tied to water like the Ganga — even setting faith aside for a moment: the land on which a river flows — that belongs to it. Who gave you the right to give that land of the river to someone else? Or — it's 100 metres wide so let's make it 5 metres, that's fine, let's build apartments here — and you keep shrinking the rivers until you make them a drain. And then when a flood comes you raise an outcry. So with such questions, Tarun Bharat Sangh moved from ponds to rivers.

Quote (original): Hum phir west se aate hain idhar center ki taraf toh hamara Jaipur ke aas paas kaam hai. Toh Jaipur ka ilaaka Dhundhadh kahalata hai ye poora jitna hai. Toh Dhundhadh mein khara paani hai ek samasya hai. In jo industrialization badh raha hai, jameenen kam hoti ja rahi hain aur ye sab cheezen toh yahan par hum paani ke muddon ka jo rural Jaipur hai vahan hamara kaam hai. Ye apne aap mein ek alag agro climatic zone hai. Phir aap east ki taraf jab jaate hain toh Chambal ka agro climatic zone jo hai Dholpur aur Bharatpur. Dholpur aur Karauli aur Dholpur. Karoli Dholpur aur usmein Bharatpur mein hamara kaam hai.
Quote (translated): Coming from the west towards the centre, our work is around Jaipur. The Jaipur area is called Dhundhadh — all of it. In Dhundhadh, brackish water is a problem. With industrialization increasing, land is decreasing — and on these issues of water in rural Jaipur, that is where our work is. This is itself a separate agro-climatic zone. Then when you go east, there is the Chambal agro-climatic zone — Dholpur and Bharatpur. Dholpur and Karauli and Dholpur. We have work in Karauli, Dholpur, and Bharatpur.

Quote (original): Toh idhar toh ma'am koi kinne chuni hai toh ladies mein hai jo bhi baani. Jets mein bhi hai aise toh TV vagairah. Hota hi hue haan. Nahi nahi saman mein pehle pehle main khane mein yaar gaadi pareshani se dhavaiya toh paani chaad le. Janda pehle kya hai ek hua thi pehle apne kuen the. Toh kuen mein kya hai main dekha hoon jaise upar se billi kabutar ye mar jaate the. Ab auraten jaati na toh vahan pe vo kheenchti thi paani — toh vo balti daal ke vo kheench ke aur usko le aati thi. Toh usmen kabutar hai, saanp hai, billi hai — jo bhi hai na — vo kachra pad jata tha aur bimari hone ka kaaran ye bhi tha.
Quote (translated): Here ma'am — whoever is counted — in ladies whatever illness comes. In Jats too there is TB and such. It does happen yes. No no — for things earlier — earlier in food — with difficulty of vehicle troubles one would carry water. What it was earlier — there used to be wells. Now in the wells — I have seen — like from above cats and pigeons would die (fall in). Now when women would go — they would pull the water there — they'd drop the bucket and pull and bring it. In that — pigeon, snake, cat — whatever was there — garbage would fall in — and that too was a reason for illness.

Quote (original): Ye tumhen je tum Google it out na. Ab toh ghat ke executive hoga. Toh mil jayenge kaafi iss pe likha hua hai ki Rajasthan aur mere khyaal se ye sirf Rajasthan ki baat nahi hai aaj pe chal ye tum kisi bhi state ko jab logi toh abhi cheezen badal gayi hain abhi cheezen badli hain kyunki pehle kya hota tha ki jis ilaake mein samaj ya jo aapka janm ho raha hai. Toh aap uss ilaake ki topography se prabhavit hote the, aap uss ilaake ke climate se prabhavit hote the, aap uss climate aap uss ilaake ke geography se prabhavit hote the. Aur usi ke hisab se aapki aadatein banti thi, aapke vyavhaar banti thi, aapke phir paramparaayen banti thi aur vahi phir aapke ek aap usko lifestyle jeevan shaili bhi ban jaati hain jisko maarneta hai hum kehte hain. Isliye ye jo zones hain isliye toh vo bahut mayne rakhte hain. Agar aapko kisi ko history mein dekhna hai, samajhna hai ki vo kahan se evolve ho ke aaya hai.
Quote (translated): You can Google this. Now there will be plenty of content available on it. A lot has been written — about Rajasthan — and I think this is not just about Rajasthan. Apply this to any state today. Things have changed now, because earlier what would happen: the society or the community that was being born in an area — you were influenced by the topography of that area, by the climate of that area, by the geography of that area. And accordingly your habits formed, your behavior formed, your traditions formed, and those then became your lifestyle — what we call 'jeewan shaili.' That is why these zones matter enormously. If you want to see someone historically, understand where they evolved from—

Quote (original): Toh kyunki vo vyakti vahan se paida hua hai. Unka apna ek itihaas raha hai. Vo uss jameen par lade hain, mare hain. Achha ladai ka matlab talwar vali bhi ladai ho sakti hai aur ladai ka matlab prakriti se bhi ladai ho sakti hai. Kabhi akal hai, kabhi baadh hai, kabhi banjar jamin hai, kuchh bhi ho sakta hai. Vo usko survive kar raha hai, theek hai na? Toh vo jo jipsa hoti hai na, toh jab aap Jaisalmer jaati hain aur Jaisalmer ke logon se jab aap baat karte hain toh you find that they are so harmful, matlab hospitality toh Western Rajasthan ki toh jaanti ho na kitne meethhe log hain ye sab cheezen hain. Uska ek bada reason hai.
Quote (translated): Because that person was born there. They have their own history. They have fought and died on that land. 'Fight' here can mean battle with a sword, but it can also mean fighting nature — sometimes drought, sometimes floods, sometimes barren land, anything. They are surviving it, right? And you know that hospitality — when you go to Jaisalmer and speak to the people there, you find that they are so warm — the hospitality of Western Rajasthan, you know how sweet these people are — all these things are there. There is a big reason for that.

Quote (original): Aur vahi agar thoda bahut uske paas paani hai aur vah aage jaake usko kaise bhi sinch leta hai, kaise bhi marmara ke karta hai, March mein ole pad jaate hain. Aadhi fasal khatam ho jaati hai toh yahan usne June mein karz liya tha. Wo doob gaya phir usne aur karj liya. Pehle jo kaam sau rupaye mein ho jata tha wo do sau rupaye mein kiya. Do sau rupaye ko usne kaise bhi kar karke usne kiya. Uski teen sau rupaye ki fasal hui toh aadhi fasal vo le mein barbaad ho gayi. Dedh sau rupaye ka wo khatam ho gaya. Uske paas bacha kya? Kyonki jis jisse karja liya hai vo bhi toh apna interest lega. Vo bhi toh maangega. Toh kya toh tumhare paas khane ko bacha? Kya tumhare paas bechne ko bacha? Kya tumhare parivar ke liye bacha?
Quote (translated): And even if he has a little water and somehow manages to irrigate, somehow barely makes it work — in March the hailstones fall. Half the crop is finished. So here he took a loan in June. He drowned in it, then took another loan. What earlier cost a hundred rupees, now costs two hundred. He somehow managed those two hundred. His crop came to three hundred rupees worth — but half the crop was destroyed in the hailstones. He was left with 150 rupees. What remained for him? Because the one from whom he took the loan will demand his interest too. He will ask for it. So what is left for you to eat? What is left for you to sell? What is left for your family?

Quote (original): Theek hai na? Vo bhi nayi nayi mausami bimariyon ke kaaran unka bhi ekdam aisi mauten hoti hain ki vo pandrah bachche bhi ek raat mein gayab ho jayenge, mar jaate hain, pata bhi nahi chalta hai. Theek hai? Toh hota kya hai? Tumhare paas 100 bheede thi? Toh 100 bheede aaj bhi vo bachche deti hain, ye hota 50 bachchon ki bajay tumhare paas 15 bachche hain, 15 mein se bhi paanch mar gaye, tumhare paas 10 bachche. Tumhare paas abhi kuchh nuksan nahi hua. Tumhari future income le lo. Kyonki vo bachche agle saal tum bhejte. Jab vo pachaas bachche bechte ek hazaar ka bhi rukta jo ki aisa kam se kam teen hazaar ka hota hai agar pachaas bachche bech lete toh dedh lakh tumhari income hoti lekin ab tumhare paas sirf das bachche hain teen ke saath tees hazaar income ho gayi dedh lakh se tees hazaar pe pahunch gaye jo ki agle saal tumhari income hoti. Voh loss tumhara aa gaya.
Quote (translated): Right? And because of new seasonal diseases, there are deaths among them too — those fifteen young can disappear in a single night, they die, you don't even know. Right? So what happens? You had 100 sheep. Your 100 sheep still give young today — but instead of 50 young you have 15, and of those 15, five also died — you have 10 young. You have had no loss yet — take your future income. Because those young you would sell next year. When selling those fifty young — even at a thousand each — which is actually at least three thousand — if you sold fifty young your income was one and a half lakhs. But now you only have ten young — at three thousand each — income became thirty thousand. From one and a half lakhs you have come to thirty thousand — which was your income for next year. That loss has hit you.

Quote (original): Nahi nahi, ye wave vali problem nahi hai, ye toh denial vali problem hai.
Quote (translated): No no, this is not a 'wave' problem, this is a denial problem.

Quote (original): Ye zyada bimaard hoon. Matki atki unse matki le jao tha anda se khet mein subha le jao tha chara ka chamosa mein. Toh yaad yaad se maine de de jao se phir jaar pakade baith jao saare paani.
Quote (translated): Yes, more sick then. Carrying the pot — take the pot and go — carry it from inside to the field in the morning — for the bundle of fodder. Then with aching body, pour out (the water) and then just sit holding the joints — from all that water carrying.

Quote (original): Bhai le jao hai saab ji humein bata hi nahi bhai be kotmal jao hai saab bimaar nahi bhai light gayi. Bimaar bhi jaaye chhe par phir bhi kaam toh karni pade jo khet ko bhi karni pade jo khaaba.
Quote (translated): Brother, take it — sir we don't even say brother — go even without strength sir — not sick brother, the electricity went. Even when sick you go but still work has to be done — the farm work too has to be done — for food.

Quote (original): Nahi jab paani ka problem aati hai toh sharir mein aur problems aati hai. Jab aap itna lena paani lene jaate the — pehle pehle ka batao. Pehle ka batao, abhi toh achha hai.
Quote (translated): No — when there is a water problem, other problems come in the body. When you used to go so much to fetch water — tell about the earlier time. Tell about before — now it is good.

Quote (original): Toh ye system hai aur ladkiyan hain hamare jaise abhi kai yahan se school mein jaati hai Nehra Sarkari school mein jaati hai. Par ye abhi ye hai — ye aisa nahi hai bhai unki saath mein koi galat ya koi chheda chhadi — aisa kuchh bhi problem nahi hai.
Quote (translated): So this is the system. And girls — many from here go to school at Nehra Government school. But right now it's not like there is anything wrong done to them or any teasing — there is no such problem.

Quote (original): Aur ya 15 ko toh vo apne se pehle se vo maan ke baithte hain ki humko bahanebaazi kyunki vo bachne ke liye — ki bhaiya inke liye aaya hai inke liye aaya hai — aur utna hi vo kar lete hain. Toh unke paas hota bhi nahi aur jo form pehle laga diya toh unko de diya, nahi toh unko nahi. Toh vo problem jo aap aankud mein baat karte hain na — toh vo sarkar aankud mein isi hi baat karte khel karte hain. Ki humne iss kisaanon ko karj maaf kar diya itna.
Quote (translated): And even those 15 — they sit already thinking they have an excuse — because to protect themselves — 'brother this came for these people, it came for these people' — and they only do that much. So they also don't have enough and whoever filed the form first, they gave to them, otherwise not. So the problem you speak about in data — the government plays this same game in data — 'we waived this much loan for this many farmers.'

Quote (original): Bhai ye bhi toh ho sakta hai na? Aap keh do ki kisi gaanv mein iss gaanv mein toh paani nahi hai, 50 ghar mein paani nahi hai aur vo ho raha hai. Aur usi jal jan jeevan mission pe usi ka har ghar jan dikha raha hai, 100% certification hai. Toh aapke bhi sawal bole, sarkari aapke peeche pad gayi. Kahan se keh diya tumne? Kaisi credibility hai? Kaisi keh sakte ho tum ye? Phir tum kahoge ki sahab humne hamara source vo hai. Vo kaisi credible source hai? Toh vo sawal. Data kya ho sakta hai vo toh vo toh shayad hum dekh sakte hain. Data credible kitna hoga ki hum usko use kar sakte hain vo bhi ek bada.
Quote (translated): Brother, this can also happen — you say there is no water in this village, in 50 homes there is no water, and this is happening. But on Jal Jeevan Mission, it shows har ghar jal — 100% certification. Then questions come to you too, the government is after you. Where did you say that from? What credibility? How can you say this? Then you say: sir, our source is this. What kind of credible source is that? So that question. What data can be — perhaps we can see that. How credible will the data be so that we can use it — that is also a big matter.

Quote (original): But mujhe lagta hai ki agar public policy koi padh raha hai aur usko policy kaise banti hai, policy ka kagaz kaise banta hai, toh JJM padhna chahie. Jameen pe kya hua vo ek alag cheez hai. Kyonki again public policy jab hoti hai toh document aur implement. And as a document it's wonderful document. Sachchi gaali de rahi hun. Mere lagta hai ki bas yahi pura samatamulak samaj ka nirman isi kagaz se ho jaayega.
Quote (translated): But I feel — if someone is studying public policy and wants to understand how policy is made, how a policy document is written, they should read JJM. What happened on the ground is a separate matter. Because again — public policy has two parts — document and implement. And as a document, it's a wonderful document. Honestly, I feel like cursing. I feel like just this one paper will build the entire equitable society.

Quote (original): Unhone Johar ki jo importance thi — pyaas ek purush ko bhi utni hi lagti hai aur mahila ko bhi utni hi lagti hai. This is the concept that he understood. And that's something, that's the beauty — and they knew ki pyaas dono ko lagti hai. Lekin iss kaam ke liye mahilaon ko involve karne mein energy double lagne vali hai. But unhone kiya.
Quote (translated): They understood the importance of the Johar — thirst is felt as much by a man as by a woman. This is the concept that he understood. And that's something, that's the beauty — and they knew that thirst is felt by both. But to involve women in this work would take double the energy. But they did it.

Quote (original): Aur aisa nahi tha ki vo pehle din hi aakar bole ki bhai, humare yahan pe meeting mein jo mahila aayegi vo ghunghat nahi karegi, kyunki hum parda ke khilaf hain — nahi. Unhone bahut hi khubsurati se — pehle vo uske andar, us cheez ke andar — jaise unhone pehle use apnaya, phir use badla. And that is the right thing to do.
Quote (translated): And it was not as if they came on the very first day and said: brother, the women who come to our meetings will not wear the ghunghat because we are against purdah — no. They did it very beautifully — first they went within it, within that thing — like they first adopted it, then changed it. And that is the right thing to do.

Quote (original): Jab meri dadi sab paani khana khate the toh haath dhote the aur usi mein thaali mein vo uss paani ko peete the — kabhi phenka nahi. Haan, kyunki unka kehna tha ki anaj hai aur paani hai, toh haath usi thaali mein dho ke usko peena hota tha, waste nahi karna tha. So jab mere mother ka time aaya — maine dekha ki unhone thaali mein hand wash kiya, par unhone aisi jagah daala aur phir kaha ki anaj hai, chidiya kha legi. Theek hai? Zameen pe phirka. Aur phir aai meri generation — jinhonne thaali mein jhoota chhoda aur haath dhoye sink mein. Ye humare life styles the.
Quote (translated): When my grandmother used to eat, after eating they would wash their hands and drink that same water in the same plate — never wasted it. Yes, because their belief was: there is grain and there is water, so you wash your hands in that same plate and drink it, don't waste it. So when my mother's time came — I saw that she washed hands in the plate but poured it on a spot saying: there is grain, the birds will eat it. Right? Thrown on the ground. And then came my generation — who left leftover food in the plate and washed hands in the sink. These were our lifestyles.

Quote (original): Uski apni kabiyat hai. Uska apna alag anubhav hai. Uski apni alag prasthabhoomi hai jismein vo rah raha hai, vo rah rahi hai. Uski roz ki aadat hai. Usko pehle bolte hain.
Quote (translated): They have their own capacity. Their own unique experience. Their own unique background in which they live. Their daily habit. First speak to them on their level.

Quote (original): Aap jaise kisaan nidhi dete hain kisaanon ko — toh ek kisaan ko 5000, 2000 — aur unke 15 bigha mein 2000 kya hoga? Aur aankda kya jaata hai ki humne itne lakh kisht aaj humne bheja. Vo upar dikhate neeche tak vo cheez specific nahi hai.
Quote (translated): Like Kisan Nidhi (PM farmer fund) is given to farmers — one farmer gets 5000, 2000 — and for someone with 15 bigha what will 2000 do? And the figure that goes out: 'today we sent this many lakh installments.' It shows above but down below that thing is not specific.

Quote (original): Toh jo ye jaise maan lo aap bata rahe ho ki inke ghar mein paani hai toh ye unka khud ka khudwaya wala borewell hota tha. Haan haan haan, paise unke paas hain. Aur phir vo aur logon ko agar unki marzi hoti thi toh lene dete aur nahi toh phir apni hukum vo kar dete.
Quote (translated): So what you're saying — in their house there was water because they had their own self-drilled borewell. Yes yes yes, they had money. And then they would let others take water if they felt like it — otherwise they would exercise their authority as they pleased.

Quote (original): Kyonki jisko help leni hai usko bhi nahi pata hai ki mere ko help mil sakti hai. Aur main kis cheez pe help lun usko nahi pata hai. Aur jisko help deni hai usko pata hi nahi hai ki iss pe help deni hai. Yahan toh abhi jisko dena hai usko nahi pata jisko lena hai usko nahi pata.
Quote (translated): Because the one who needs help doesn't know that help can be available. And they don't know what to seek help for. And the one who has to give help doesn't even know what help to give. Right now, the one who needs to give doesn't know and the one who needs to receive doesn't know.

Quote (original): Jisse usko dusra karza nahi lena pade. Kyonki kisaan toh kheti karega hi karega. Bhaiya tum use nahi paisa doge toh tum kya soch rahe ho kisaan kheti nahi karega. Usne jeevan bhar kuchh aur kiya hi nahi hai. Vo kheti ke alawa kuchh kar nahi sakta hai. Bhaad jaayega toh majdoori karni padegi.
Quote (translated): So that they don't have to take another loan. Because the farmer will farm regardless. Brother, if you don't give him money, what do you think — the farmer won't farm? He has done nothing else his whole life. He cannot do anything other than farming. If the crop fails he will have to do labour.

Quote (original): Toh mazdoori toh vo apne khet mein hi kar le. Toh phir vo aur karza leke karega. Yahan responsibility hai, speed kaam na. Vo kahan form bharega, kiski paas jaayega, kab uske paas logon aayega. Yahan vo apne gaanv mein kisi ke paas jaayega, aapke aur mere paas. Hum uske dost hain, hum usko paisa de denge.
Quote (translated): So let him do that labour on his own field. Then he will take another loan. Here — responsibility, speed, these don't work. Where will he fill a form, who will he go to, when will people come to him. Here he will go to someone in his own village — to you and me. We are his friends, we will give him money.

Quote (original): Madad main bataun aapko — unke upar koi pressure nahi hai. Yahan aate hain jaise apne ek doctor aata hai Amit Devandha — vahan se aata hai apne Kashi Ganga Jamuna petrol pump se. Toh vo aata hai — wahan pe aata hai toh vo usko yahan pe aa jata hai — vo toh khud aata nahi — uske neeche phir koi hai na compounder vagairah — vo market mein ghoomte hain, yahan pe gaon mein ghoomte hain. Toh vo aaj jinka kehna maante hain vo kar dete hain — kahin ka phone hi nahi uthate. Aur abhi abhi jis banda ko phone karo toh vo kehte hain 'haan sahab main bhej raha hoon' — lekin vo koi aaj din tak nahi aate.
Quote (translated): Help — let me tell you — there is no pressure on them (the doctors). Here comes one doctor — Amit Devandha — he comes from near the Kashi Ganga Jamuna petrol pump. He comes — he comes there — but he himself doesn't come here — under him there is a compounder and others — they roam in the market, roam here in the village. So whoever they feel like listening to, they do for them — they don't pick up calls from others. And right now whoever you call, they say 'yes sir, I am sending someone' — but nobody has come till today.

Quote (original): Main diya si alaiyan kati hoi si. Alaiyan bahut hoi si. Nahi thoda hai main toh bhajan samne samne se. Ab toh kaise pocho bhi le aao toh bathroom mein jaisa bhi paani le se. Bada su le le se. Aajkal koi nikhale ko nahi cheez toh. Niklo. Phule pankha mein so jaaye aise mein so jaaye.
Quote (translated): I used to get eczema/skin sores (alaiyan). Lots of eczema. Now it's a little — I manage myself. Nowadays even if you ask — just bring it and there's water like in a bathroom. Take as much as you want. Nowadays there is nothing to drive you out. Go out. Sleep under the fan in flowers (comfort) — sleep like that.

Quote (original): Theek hai. Tarun Bharat Singh jo hai vo kareeb abhi vartaman May mein ikyaavan saal ka ho jaayega. Toh unnees sau pachhattar mein sanghathan ka janm hua. Aur jab shuruaat hui thi tab alag alag muddon par paryavaraneeya muddon par kaam karna hai aur yeh sab shuruat hui lekin ek samay ke saath unnees sau pachasi tak aate aate mere khyaal se Tarun Bharat Sangh ki disha ban gayi thi ki hum sirf paani par hi kaam karenge.
Quote (translated): Alright. Tarun Bharat Sangh is currently — by this May — completing 51 years. The organization was born in 1975. When it began, the idea was to work on various environmental issues, and all of that started, but over time, by 1985 I think, the direction of Tarun Bharat Sangh had been set: that we would work only on water.

Quote (original): They are not — because ab mata-pita ke dhyan saamne hai. Aaj agar vo main khud itni frustrated hoon ki vo bachcha kuchh bhi bol raha hai, I don't give a shit, because main frustrated hun inside. But ab vo bachcha bol raha hai — main andar se heal hoon, main andar se satisfied hoon, main andar se khush hoon — toh main usko tok sakti hoon ki 'bhai tu ne kya bola, kaise bola, tujhe pata hai bado aur chhoto se kaise baat karte hain.'
Quote (translated): They are not — because now parents' attention is there. Today if I myself am so frustrated that whatever that child is saying, I don't give a damn, because I am frustrated inside. But now when the child says something — I am healed inside, I am satisfied inside, I am happy inside — then I can correct them: 'hey, what did you say, how did you say it, do you know how to speak to elders and youngsters.'

Quote (original): Toh main bolti hai ki 'tune taanke toh gine par ye taanke se — na taanke ne mera jeevan — taanke ne meri zindagi jeene layak bana di — isko tu kaise ginegi?' I was stunned. Maine kaha kya? Matlab? Toh bole — ye dhor jaisi zindagi thi. Dhor — pashu jo hain vahan, bhains jo hai, jaanvar ki dhor jaisi zindagi thi. 'Ye bhi bhale hain — unko subah koi paani dene wala hota hai, subah nikaal dete hain, khuli charti hai, khati hai, raat ko aati hai, toh main ise paani pilaati.' And she was talking about data.
Quote (translated): Then she says: 'You counted the tankas but these tankas — the tanka has made my life — the tanka has made my life worth living — how will you count that?' I was stunned. I said: what? Meaning? She said: this was a life like that of dhor. Dhor — the animals there, the buffaloes, the cattle — it was a life like an animal's life. 'These are also better off — someone gives them water in the morning, they are let out in the morning, they graze freely, they eat, they come back at night, and I give them water.' And she was talking about data.
